name: Lake Chatyr-Kul
near: There are no permanent villages on the shore. The nearest places with accommodation are the Tash-Rabat caravanserai with its yurt camps (on the north side, over the Panda Pass, a 2-day horse/hiking trek of 44 km round trip) and the Torugart border/customs complex on the highway south of the lake. The town of Naryn is the base for the trip (about 2 h by car to Tash-Rabat). The earlier “Torugart ~10.6 km” is an OSM marker for the settlement at the checkpoint, not a tourist locality.
elev: 3,530 m (Nomad's Land, TripAdvisor); too.kg and Advantour round it to 3,500 m.
short: Chatyr-Kul is the third-largest lake in Kyrgyzstan (≈153–160 km²) at an elevation of 3,530 m between the At-Bashy and Torugart-Too ranges near the Chinese border; it is endorheic, fishless, and a Ramsar site within the Karatal-Japyryk Nature Reserve.
desc: A high-mountain endorheic lake of glacial origin lies in an intermontane basin between the At-Bashy Range and Torugart-Too, with the Bishkek–Kashgar highway running alongside it via the Torugart Pass. The area is 153.5 km² with a shoreline of 58 km (TripAdvisor) or 160 km² (Advantour), and the depth is up to 16.5–20 m. About 17 rivers flow into the lake, of which only one is permanent; there are no fish. For most of the year the lake is covered with ice: the average annual temperature is about −5 °C, down to −50 °C in winter, in summer the air warms up to +24 °C and the water to no more than +10 °C. The shores are marshy, and the vegetation is low, coarse grass. The lake is part of the Karatal-Japyryk State Nature Reserve and a Ramsar wetland: thousands of migratory birds stop here in summer, so you must not approach the water itself. The name is translated as “Heavenly Lake” / “roof lake”. A visit is possible only with a border-zone permit.
guide: The best way to see Chatyr-Kul is a two-day horse trek from Tash-Rabat over the Panda Pass (about 4,000 m): from the saddle the basin with the huge lake and the Torugart-Too range opens up in full. You spend the night in a yurt by the lake, and at dawn, if you are lucky, you will see flocks of migratory birds — this is a Ramsar site, so do not approach the water and keep your distance from the nesting areas. There are no fish in the lake and the ice stays for most of the year, so it can snow even in July. You will not be let in without a permit: arrange it in advance through CBT Naryn together with the trip to Tash-Rabat.
see: The panorama of the basin from the Panda Pass (≈4,000 m) on the trek from Tash-Rabat; migratory and waterbirds (Ramsar site); the snowy Torugart-Too range on the Chinese border; marshy shores and mineral springs (Nomad's Land); along the highway — a view of the lake on the way to Torugart.
skip: You have no time to arrange a border-zone permit (up to 1–2 weeks). You want to swim or go up to the water — the shore is a reserve and marshy. You tolerate altitudes of 3,500–4,000 m and unpredictable weather with snow in any month poorly.
diff: Moderate: the horse/hiking trek Tash-Rabat – Chatyr-Kul is 44 km over 2 days, gain ~1,350 m, the Panda Pass is about 4,000 m (snoezelsontheroad; CBT Naryn — “moderate”); on foot one way is 5–7 h (TripAdvisor). By car on the highway — easy, but only with a permit and within what is allowed.
when: July–August (the lake is under ice most of the year; snow is possible at any time of year — TripAdvisor). The yurt camps at Tash-Rabat operate in summer.
hours: Border zone and nature reserve: visits only with a border-zone permit; access to the shoreline is restricted to protect birds (TripAdvisor). There is no schedule.
daytime: Dawn and morning — birdwatching, calm weather, a clear view of Torugart-Too; on the trek set out early to cross the Panda Pass before the weather worsens in the afternoon (editorial).
how: 1) On foot/on horseback: from Naryn by car to Tash-Rabat (~2 h), then the trek over the Panda Pass to the lake and back the next day (CBT Naryn). 2) By car: along the Naryn–Torugart highway, which runs along the lake (Nomad's Land; central-asia.guide mentions a border checkpoint on the highway) — only with a permit, and stops and turn-offs to the shore are restricted.
needcar: Yes: there is no public transport to Tash-Rabat (snoezelsontheroad) — a taxi/transfer from Naryn; then a horse or on foot; or a car on the highway with a permit.
self: Partly: the permit is mandatory (CBT Naryn, tour.too.kg); the trek over Panda is not recommended without a guide — snoezelsontheroad calls the guide “indispensable”. Independent driving on the highway is possible only with a permit.
roadtype: To Tash-Rabat — the paved Naryn–Torugart highway and a dirt road to the caravanserai; then a horse/hiking trail over the Panda Pass. The Torugart highway along the lake is a main road (Bishkek–Kashgar direction).
traveltime: Naryn – Tash-Rabat ~2 h by car (snoezelsontheroad); Tash-Rabat – Chatyr-Kul 5–7 h on foot/on horseback one way (TripAdvisor); the whole trek is 2 days.
stay: A yurt camp on the lake shore as part of a CBT Naryn tour; yurt camps at Tash-Rabat — 1,500–2,000 som/person with breakfast and dinner, cash payment (snoezelsontheroad, 2025–2026). Also guesthouses in Naryn (CBT Naryn).
net: Not confirmed on operators’ coverage maps. On the trek and by the lake expect no signal; at the Torugart checkpoint a signal is possible (unconfirmed).
entry: No separate reserve fee for tourists was found. A border-zone permit is mandatory: CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn Region, one week), €35 (several regions), €50 urgent; tour.too.kg — 3,000 som (all zones, 2026); about 2,000 som according to the snoezelsontheroad report.
transfer: Marshrutka (minibus) Bishkek – Naryn — 600 som (CBT Naryn, 05.2026). Horse — 1,500 som/day, guide — 2,500 som per group (snoezelsontheroad). The cost of the CBT Naryn tour and of a taxi Naryn – Tash-Rabat is not given in the sources — check with CBT Naryn.
bring: Your border-zone permit and passport; warm and waterproof clothing (snow at any time of year), a hat, gloves; sunscreen and sunglasses; binoculars for birds; cash som; trekking shoes; an altitude-sickness first-aid kit.
warn: It is a border zone near the Chinese border — you will not be let through without a permit. Nature reserve and Ramsar site: approaching the water, disturbing birds and camping on the shore outside permitted places are not allowed. The altitude is 3,530 m, the Panda Pass ~4,000 m; the weather changes abruptly. The existence of a road along the lake does not give you the right to drive freely down to the shore.
food: In the yurt camps at Tash-Rabat and at the lake — home-cooked dinner and breakfast (included in the 1,500–2,000 som); typical dishes are shorpo, beshbarmak, boorsok, kumis (editorial).
reviews: TripAdvisor: 4.6/5, 7 reviews, No. 2 of 3 in At-Bashy (as of 07.10.2026). Google Maps: 4.8/5, 22 ratings (as of 03.10.2026, catalog check). Pros — powerful mountains, few tourists, inexpensive yurts with good food. Cons — unpredictable weather, a hard day on the trek, you cannot go up to the water, little information from operators in Naryn.
p.sum: There are two ways to Chatyr-Kul, both only with a border-zone permit. The best is from Tash-Rabat on foot or on horseback over the pass (≈3,996 m): 21.6 km one way, a night in a yurt camp by the lake, and back the next day (2 days; a horse at Tash-Rabat ≈1,500 som/day + a guide 2,500 som per group). The second is along the Naryn–Torugart highway, which runs along the southern shore: views from the car, but swamps and reserve rules prevent you from driving up to the water, and the permit is checked at the posts. The base is the yurt camps of Tash-Rabat (1,500–2,000 som with breakfast and dinner; Ak-Sai — from $65) or Naryn; fill up your tank in Naryn.

p.season: June — snowy pass and swamp; July–August — the best window, birds nesting, about 0 °C at night; September — frosts, snow; October–May — the Torugart highway is open, but the lake is frozen (down to −50 °C), the trek is closed. After rain the shores turn into a swamp (LP).
p.budget.economy: ≈9,000–13,000 som/person for 3 days: marshrutka 600×2, taxi Naryn–Tash-Rabat (by arrangement, split among 4), permit 3,000, yurt 2 nights 3,000–4,000, horse 1,500×2 + a share of the guide; or on foot.
p.budget.comfort: ≈$300–500/person: CBT/Eurasia tour (from $500 for 2 days at Eurasia) or a car with a driver + Ak-Sai camp $65–85 + a horse $15/hour
p.permits: A border-zone permit is mandatory (border zone of the At-Bashy District near the Chinese border). Ways to get it: 1) tour.too.kg — 3,000 som (all border zones) / $35 for the Kel-Suu–Kok-Kiya–Chatyr-Kul zone; 5–7 working days; office at 105/3 Isanov St., Bishkek (2026). 2) CBT Naryn — €30 (Naryn Region only, ~1 week), €35 (several regions), €50 urgent in 2 working days (stage 1); Nomad's Land: from Naryn it is fastest — in a few days, via Bishkek — up to 2 weeks. Step by step: (1) send a scan of your passport and the trip dates (WhatsApp/form); (2) pay a 50% prepayment; (3) the Border Service reviews it for ~1 week; (4) pick up the paper original in Bishkek or Naryn (or via the guide/tour — then a copy of the passport is sent a few days earlier). The permit is valid for up to 1 month. It is checked at the military posts on the Kyndy pass/at the entrance to the Ak-Sai valley (2 posts per Eurasia Travel) — you need the original permit with a stamp and your passport. Photographing the posts is forbidden. No fee for entering the lake area/valley was found. Chatyr-Kul is part of the Karatal-Japyryk nature reserve (Ramsar): no separate tourist fee was found; approaching the water and disturbing the birds are not allowed.
p.access: The trek is only for the fit (4,000 m); with children and older people, the view of the lake can be had from a car on the Torugart highway (with a permit). A stroller — only from the car. A dog on the trek — not advisable (nature reserve, shepherd dogs).
